heroHeadline: US-Iran Deal Still Unsigned Day 3 After Decision Day; White House Denies Leaked Memo; 'Strong Inspections' Language Emerges — Colombia Election 4 Days Away, Race in Near-Tie in Some Polls
heroSubtitle: May 27, 2026 — Three days after Trump's self-declared 'decision day' (May 24) on Iran, the US-Iran deal remains unsigned. The White House denied a leaked Iranian state TV memo on deal terms ('not true'), while Trump said negotiations are advancing with 'strong inspections' language for Iran's nuclear program. Rubio indicated deal finalization could take 'a couple of days.' On May 26, US military forces conducted 'self-defense strikes' targeting Iranian missile launch sites and boats near the Strait of Hormuz — even as deal talks continued — with Iran's IRGC reporting 25 vessels transited the Strait under Iranian oversight in 24 hours. The 14-point MOU framework (Phase 1: Hormuz opens in 30 days, Iran oil sales resume; Phase 2: 60-day nuclear talks) remains the public baseline. In Colombia, with 4 days to the May 31 first-round election, the CNC poll (May 16-22) shows a near-technical tie between Cepeda (33.4%) and De la Espriella (30.9%), though Invamer still shows Cepeda with a wider lead (44.6% vs. 31.6%). The ELN's pre-election ceasefire is holding. A June 21 runoff is virtually certain — and whether Cepeda or De la Espriella faces the runoff ballot determines whether Colombia's peace architecture survives. Lebanon's 45-day ceasefire extension remains under strain: the Pentagon security track meeting is scheduled for May 29, the first military-to-military bilateral meeting — UNIFIL has now logged 10,000+ violations since the April 16 ceasefire began. Ukraine talks remain stalled with no new round scheduled.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
